newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to meet Chechen leader soon in Moscow.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to meet Chechen leader soon in Moscow.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin agreed on Friday during a telephone conversation with the leader of Russia's breakaway Chechnya republic to meet him soon in Moscow, the Kremlin said.
"During the talks issues of relations between Moscow and (the Chechen capital) Grozny were discussed," a statement issued by Yeltsin's press service said.
"An agreement was reached that a face-to-face meeting will take place in the near future in Moscow," it said.

Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said on Thursday that Russia was concerned that documents signed under a peace deal between the federal government and Chechen President Aslan Maskhadov were not being put into effect.
Moscow agreed a ceasefire with Chechnya's separatist leaders a year ago after 21 months of vying for control of the North Caucasus territory. Tens of thousands of people were killed in the fighting.

But the peace process has been hampered by an outstanding disagreement over the status of the republic. Maskhadov says it is independent and Yeltsin insists it is and must remain part of the Russian Federation.

"This will be a difficult conversation," Yastrzhembsky said, referring to the presidents' planned meeting. He added that Yeltsin would emphasise to Maskhadov the need to restore the rule of law in Chechnya.
Hostage-taking has become a huge problem in the turbulent Caucasus region since last August. Several foreigners, including two Britons, are still missing after being seized by gunmen.

The abductions have hampered Chechnya's efforts to improve its image and to attract desperately needed funds to rebuild its shattered economy. Maskhadov on Thursday offered an amnesty to hostage takers if they release their victims by August 10.
Ivan Rybkin, secretary of Russia's Security Council, visited Grozny on Thursday to prepare for the meeting.

He played down comments by Russian First Deputy Fuel and Energy Minister Sergei Kiriyenko on Wednesday that Moscow might build a section of oil pipeline around Chechnya because of problems sealing an oil transport deal with Grozny.
